text: Build in this order: eval dataset, then monitoring, then incident response plan, then model card. Eval comes first because everything after depends on knowing what working correctly actually means.
Fifteen to twenty cases, each with a realistic input and a correct output. Include a few deliberately hard cases — fifteen easy cases that all pass tells you nothing you didn't already believe.

Monitoring doesn't need a production platform — log every call's input, output, timestamp, and one real chart. Then write the incident response plan for your actual failure mode, specific to what you built.
Fill in the real six model card sections for your actual feature, using your actual evaluation numbers. If a section feels hard to fill in honestly, that's useful information about your system.
Four deliverables, built in order, each depending on the one before it. Next up: wrapping up and presenting what you built.
